full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

dependencies.statement: For every natural n and every continuous real function f on the Euclidean space R^n with compact topological support, f is integrable for Lebesgue measure.

origin.revision: Frozen task Mathlib environment; selected declarations inspected with read_mathlib. Public comparison sources are separately versioned in the reference where used.

lean.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Integrable f
lean.proof:
intro n f hf hc
exact hf.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport hc

dependencies.justification: Specialize the inspected native theorem to scalar real functions and Euclidean volume; Euclidean volume is finite on compact sets. No extra support or positivity condition.

dependencies.statement: Let n be natural, X=R^n with Euclidean Lebesgue measure, F,D:R→X→R, t0∈R, s a neighborhood of t0, and b:X→R. Suppose F(t,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable for t sufficiently near t0, F(t0,·) is integrable, D(t0,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable, b is integrable, and for almost every x and all t∈s both |D(t,x)|≤b(x) and HasDerivAt (r↦F(r,x)) D(t,x) t hold. Then D(t0,·) is integrable and HasDerivAt (t↦∫x F(t,x) dx) (∫x D(t0,x) dx) t0.

dependencies.justification: Exact real scalar Euclidean specialization of the pinned theorem; every premise is retained. The common neighborhood and common majorant remain independent of x. The NL proof constructs them from uniform compact support and joint continuity.

dependencies.statement: Let n be natural, f,g:R^n→R and v∈R^n. Write D_v h(x)=fderiv R h x v and tsupport for the closure of the nonzero set. If (D_v f)g, f(D_v g), and fg are Lebesgue integrable, f is differentiable at every point of tsupport g, and g is differentiable at every point of tsupport f, then ∫x f(x)D_v g(x) dx = -∫x D_v f(x)g(x) dx.

dependencies.justification: Exact scalar real specialization, retaining all three integrability assumptions and both support-sensitive differentiability assumptions. The constant factor 1 need not itself be integrable.

dependencies.statement: For every natural n, every C^1 scalar g:R^n→R with compact topological support, and every constant v∈R^n, the scalar function x↦Dg(x)[v] is Lebesgue integrable and its integral is zero.

lean.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → Integrable (fun x => fderiv ℝ g x v) ∧ (∫ x, fderiv ℝ g x v) = 0
lean.proof:
have h_H001 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Integrable f := @YuiBasis.B001
have h_H002 : ∀ (n : ℕ) (f g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), Integrable (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x v * g x) → Integrable (fun x => f x * fderiv ℝ g x v) → Integrable (fun x => f x * g x) → (∀ x ∈ tsupport g, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) → (∀ x ∈ tsupport f, DifferentiableAt ℝ g x) → (∫ x, f x * fderiv ℝ g x v) = -(∫ x, fderiv ℝ f x v * g x) := @YuiBasis.B003
intro n g v hg hgc
rcases contDiff_one_iff_fderiv.mp hg with ⟨hgd, hgderiv⟩
have hcont : Continuous (fun x => fderiv ℝ g x v) :=
  hgderiv.clm_apply continuous_const
have hsupport : HasCompactSupport (fun x => fderiv ℝ g x v) :=
  hgc.fderiv_apply ℝ v
have hint : Integrable (fun x => fderiv ℝ g x v) :=
  h_H001 n _ hcont hsupport
have hgint : Integrable g := h_H001 n g hg.continuous hgc
refine ⟨hint, ?_⟩
have hzero : Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) =>
    fderiv ℝ (fun _ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => (1 : ℝ)) x v * g x) := by
  simpa using (integrable_zero : Integrable (fun _ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => (0 : ℝ)))
have hparts := h_H002 n (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) g v hzero
  (by simpa using hint) (by simpa using hgint)
  (by intro x hx; exact differentiableAt_const (1 : ℝ))
  (by intro x hx; exact hgd x)
simpa using hparts

dependencies.justification: Concrete derivation: C^1 implies g continuous, globally differentiable and fderiv continuous (contDiff_one_iff_fderiv/ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Evaluation at v is continuous. HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Const.lean:385–394) gives compact support of x↦Dg(x)[v]; this follows also by local equality with zero off tsupport g. Apply B001 to g and D_v g. In B003 set f=1. Its first integrand is zero, its second is D_v g, its third is g. Constants are differentiable on tsupport g, and C^1 g is differentiable on tsupport 1. B003 yields ∫ D_v g=-∫0=0. No integral of the constant 1 is asserted. Auxiliary native support/regularity facts are part of this concrete adapter, not new assumptions.

propositions.statement: The integers n,m satisfy n≥1 and m≥1, and u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth.
The fixed vector q∈R^m has Euclidean norm |q|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every t>0, |u(x,t)|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every t>0 there exists a real number a with u_tt(x,t)-Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of any choice of a is assumed.
For every pair of real times 0<s<t there is a compact set C⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for all x∉C and every r∈[s,t].
For every x∈R^n and every t>0, ⟨u(x,t),u_t(x,t)⟩=0 and ⟨u_t(x,t),u_tt(x,t)-Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t)⟩=0, where ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product.

Define e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|² and g_j(x,t)=⟨u_t(x,t),∂_{x_j}u(x,t)⟩. The real functions e, ∂_t e, g_j and ∂_{x_j}g_j are jointly smooth on R^n×(0,∞). For every t0>0 there exists a compact C⊂R^n such that, for every r∈(t0/2,3t0/2), all these functions vanish at (x,r) whenever x∉C, and their spatial topological supports are contained in C. This conclusion also holds for each inner-product term ⟨u_t,u_tt⟩, ⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩ and ⟨u_t,∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩. Indices j range from 1 to n.
For every x∈R^n and every t>0, ∂_t e(x,t)=2Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t), where e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|² and g_j(x,t)=⟨u_t(x,t),∂_{x_j}u(x,t)⟩.

For every t>0 the real spatial functions x↦e(x,t), x↦∂_t e(x,t), x↦g_j(x,t) and x↦∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t) are Lebesgue integrable on R^n for each j=1,…,n. Here e=|u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² and g_j=⟨u_t,∂_{x_j}u⟩. Each of the spatial sections of ⟨u_t,u_tt⟩, ⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩ and ⟨u_t,∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩ is also integrable.

For every t0>0 the real energy function E:(0,∞)→R defined by E(t)=∫_{R^n} (|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²) dx has derivative ∫_{R^n}∂_t e(x,t0) dx at t0, where e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². The integral is the actual Lebesgue integral and differentiation is within the open positive-time domain.
For every t>0, ∫_{R^n}∂_t e(x,t) dx=0, where e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|².

For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on R^n, and E(t)=∫_{R^n}e(x,t) dx is differentiable with E'(t)=0, where e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². Spatial squares and Laplacian use the Euclidean/Frobenius and componentwise normalizations in the original target; no conclusion is asserted at time zero.
For every natural n and every continuous real function f on the Euclidean space R^n with compact topological support, f is integrable for Lebesgue measure.

Let n be natural, X=R^n with Euclidean Lebesgue measure, F,D:R→X→R, t0∈R, s a neighborhood of t0, and b:X→R. Suppose F(t,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable for t sufficiently near t0, F(t0,·) is integrable, D(t0,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable, b is integrable, and for almost every x and all t∈s both |D(t,x)|≤b(x) and HasDerivAt (r↦F(r,x)) D(t,x) t hold. Then D(t0,·) is integrable and HasDerivAt (t↦∫x F(t,x) dx) (∫x D(t0,x) dx) t0.
For every natural n, every C^1 scalar g:R^n→R with compact topological support, and every constant v∈R^n, the scalar function x↦Dg(x)[v] is Lebesgue integrable and its integral is zero.
If f:R→Y, where Y is any real inner-product space, has derivative f' at t, then r↦‖f(r)‖² has derivative 2⟨f(t),f'⟩ at t.
For any real normed space X and real inner-product space Y, functions f,g:X→Y differentiable at x, and v∈X, D_v⟨f,g⟩(x)=⟨f(x),D_v g(x)⟩+⟨D_v f(x),g(x)⟩.
For real normed vector spaces X,Y, if f:X→Y is C^2 at x, then its second Frechet derivative is symmetric: D(Df)(x)[v][w]=D(Df)(x)[w][v] for every v,w∈X.
For real normed vector spaces X,Y, an open set s⊆X and a smooth f:X→Y on s, the derivative field x↦fderiv R f x is smooth on s.
For real normed vector spaces X,Y and f,g:X→Y, if f and g agree throughout some neighborhood of x, then their Frechet derivatives at x agree.

proof:
Global route and notation. The full target and all original hypotheses H001–H005 are retained. H002, the unit length of q, is retained but is not needed for the energy argument. The approved interpretation of compact support is uniform compact support of u-q on each closed positive-time interval, never compact support of u. No derivative, measurability, or coherent selection of the pointwise normality scalar is assumed. There is no factor 1/2 in e or E.

Use X=R^n and Y=R^m with their Euclidean inner products, and Lebesgue measure on X. In Lean X and Y may be EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) and EuclideanSpace R (Fin m), with indices 0,…,n-1 in place of 1,…,n; these are just relabelings of the same standard orthonormal coordinates and volume. On Z=X×R let Ω={(x,t):t>0}. Extend u arbitrarily outside Ω, for example by q. This is only a total representation: Ω is open, and every positive-time point has a neighborhood contained in Ω, so all derivatives there depend on the original germ by B009. There is no smoothness assertion across t=0.

For a constant direction v in a real normed domain define D_v F(z)=fderiv R F z v. Put T=(0,1) and S_j=(b_j,0), with b_j the jth standard basis vector of X. Write V=D_T u=u_t, W_j=D_{S_j}u=∂_{x_j}u, A=D_T V=u_tt and B_j=D_{S_j}W_j=∂_{x_jx_j}u. To identify a direction derivative with the indicated ordinary partial derivative, apply the chain rule to h↦z+h v, whose derivative is v. At a positive-time point the curve stays in Ω for small h. Define e=|V|²+Σ_j|W_j|² and g_j=⟨V,W_j⟩.

Outline and consumers. R001 establishes tangency and normal cancellation. R002 exports joint regularity and a common compact support window; its consumers are R004 (all spatial integrability), R005 (a single integrable majorant for differentiation), and R006 (compact support of each flux). R003 establishes the local conservation identity using tangency, norm-square differentiation, the inner product rule, and symmetry of the Hessian. R005 differentiates E using B002. R006 integrates the local identity using the zero directional integral B004 and finite integral linearity. R007 joins integrability and the derivative identity. The only non-native adapter is B004, with the direct native premises B001 and B003. B003 is used only inside that adapter and has no global port.

R001: Fix x and t>0. The curve r↦u(x,r) is smooth near t, so B005 gives the derivative of its squared norm as 2⟨u,u_t⟩. Its squared norm equals the constant 1 near t by H003. Local equality to a constant gives zero derivative (B009, or its one-dimensional evaluation), and uniqueness of the derivative gives 2⟨u,u_t⟩=0. Divide by 2. At the given point eliminate H004's existential witness a. By real inner-product symmetry and scalar bilinearity,
⟨u_t,u_tt-Σ_j∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩=⟨u_t,a u⟩=a⟨u_t,u⟩=0.
This use is pointwise and introduces no scalar field with extra regularity.

R002: B008 on the open set Ω gives smoothness of the derivative field. Evaluation of a continuous linear map at a fixed vector preserves smoothness (it is a continuous linear operation); repeating gives smoothness of V,W_j,A,B_j and all higher constant-direction derivatives used here. Inner products and squared norms in finite-dimensional Euclidean coordinates are finite sums of products of coordinate functions, so e,g_j and their derivatives and the stated inner-product terms are smooth. Their fixed-time spatial sections are smooth by the affine inclusion x↦(x,t).

Fix arbitrary t0>0. Apply H005 with s=t0/2 and t=3t0/2 to obtain a compact C. Compact subsets of Euclidean space are closed. Consequently O=(X\C)×(t0/2,3t0/2) is open and lies in Ω, and u=q throughout O. At every z∈O, u agrees near z with the constant q. B009 and the derivative of a constant give Du(z)=0. This is true on the whole open O, so the same argument applied to the derivative field gives zero second derivatives, and repetition gives every positive-order derivative zero on O. Each term listed in N002 contains positive-order derivatives of u, so all vanish there. At fixed interior time r their nonzero sets are contained in C; since C is closed their topological supports are also contained in C and are compact. No endpoint-time derivative vanishing is inferred from this window.

R003: Smoothness and B008 ensure all functions differentiated below are differentiable on Ω. For the needed mixed-partial identification set L(z)=fderiv R u z. Differentiating the continuous bilinear evaluation L(z)w at constant w gives D_v(D_w u)(z)=(fderiv R L z v)w; the term involving a derivative of w is zero. B007 applied to u, which is C² at every z∈Ω, gives equality of this expression with (fderiv R L z w)v. Thus D_T W_j=D_{S_j}V. This step uses only smoothness near z, not outside Ω.
Apply B005 along time sections to V and each W_j, differentiate the finite sum, and substitute this mixed identity:
∂_t e=2⟨V,A⟩+2Σ_j⟨W_j,D_{S_j}V⟩.
Apply B006 to the spatial section of g_j, or equivalently in direction S_j in Z:
∂_{x_j}g_j=⟨V,B_j⟩+⟨D_{S_j}V,W_j⟩.
Symmetry of the real inner product and finite-sum algebra therefore give
∂_t e-2Σ_j∂_{x_j}g_j=2⟨V,A-Σ_j B_j⟩=0
by N001. This proves N003 with the exact stated factor 2.

R004: Fix t>0. N002 provides continuous sections with topological support in a compact set. Apply B001 to every listed real function to obtain N004. This proves absolute integrability, including of the energy density, before any manipulation of its integral. It does not assert integrability of u itself.

R005: Fix t0>0. From N002 choose the common compact C and let U=(t0/2,3t0/2). The uncurried real functions F(r,x)=e(x,r) and D(r,x)=∂_t e(x,r) are jointly continuous on U×X. For every x and every r∈U, HasDerivAt (s↦F(s,x)) D(r,x) r holds by the definition of ∂_t e and smoothness. Their spatial sections are integrable by N004 and hence almost everywhere strongly measurable. They vanish outside C throughout U.

Choose R>0 large enough that C lies in the compact cube Q=[-R,R]^n; boundedness of compact subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space ensures this. The compact time interval L=[3t0/4,5t0/4] lies in U. The continuous |D| has a finite bound B≥0 on L×Q by compactness. Let b(x)=B 1_Q(x). The cube Q is closed, measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure (2R)^n, hence b is integrable. For every r in the open neighborhood s=(3t0/4,5t0/4) of t0 and every x∈Q the derivative bound |D(r,x)|≤b(x) holds by construction; for x∉Q it holds because x∉C and D(r,x)=0. Thus the bound holds everywhere and hence almost everywhere, uniformly in the same neighborhood s. The derivative hypothesis also holds everywhere on s. Section measurability holds eventually at t0 since U is a neighborhood of t0; F(t0,·) is integrable and D(t0,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable by N004. These check every premise of B002 with spatial X, F,D,t0,s,b. Its conclusion gives
HasDerivAt (r↦∫_X e(x,r) dx) (∫_X ∂_t e(x,t0) dx) t0.
Any arbitrary extension of F,D to nonpositive times is immaterial, since all these assertions are local to U; the integral agrees with the actual energy function near t0. This proves N005 for the actual finite integral.

Adapter B004 (recursive class 3 derivation): If g is C¹ with compact support, g is continuous and differentiable everywhere. The C¹ characterization gives continuity of its Frechet derivative, and evaluation at fixed v is continuous. Off tsupport g, the function agrees locally with zero, so its derivative is zero. Hence tsupport(x↦D_v g(x))⊆tsupport g, also compact. B001 gives integrability of g and D_v g. In B003 use f=1 and the given g. The three required integrands are, respectively, zero, D_v g, and g, all integrable. A constant is differentiable at every point of tsupport g, and C¹ g is differentiable at every point of tsupport 1. The conclusion is ∫D_v g=-∫0=0. The prepared Lean proof may use the exact native lemma HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply for the support inclusion; it proves this same neighborhood argument. No integrability of the constant 1 is needed.

R006: Fix t>0 and j. By N002 the spatial section x↦g_j(x,t) is smooth, hence C¹, with compact topological support. Apply B004 with v=b_j. The derivative of this spatial section evaluated at b_j is ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t) by the directional chain rule for the affine inclusion. Thus ∫_X ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t) dx=0. N004 supplies integrability of all terms, so finite-sum and scalar linearity of the Lebesgue integral apply to N003 and give
∫_X ∂_t e(x,t) dx=2Σ_j∫_X ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t) dx=0.
This is N006. It is the original integration-by-parts cancellation expressed through flux; the box, one-dimensional FTC and Fubini from the supplied proof are replaced by the already proved Mathlib integration-by-parts theorem and its B004 specialization.

R007: Given arbitrary t0>0, N004 proves integrability of e(·,t0). Substitute N006 into N005 to obtain HasDerivAt E 0 t0, which entails differentiability there and E'(t0)=0. This holds for every positive time, with the original Frobenius sum and no changed normalization. No conclusion at t=0 and no regularity of a is introduced. Constancy on (0,∞), if desired, follows from the usual mean value theorem, but is not needed as a separate dependency for the selected derivative target.
